1	// Package provenance owns the env-var contract that lets the lifecycle hook
2	// recognize a spawned agent process as part of `entire review` or `entire
3	// investigate`. Both spawn families set their own ENTIRE_*_* vars on the
4	// child agent process; the UserPromptSubmit hook reads them to tag the
5	// in-flight session with the right Kind and provenance metadata.
6	//
7	// Single source of truth for the names — review, investigate, and
8	// agentlaunch (which strips both families before spawning a fix agent) all
9	// reference this package.
10	//
11	// These names are stable API; renaming any constant is a breaking change.
12	package provenance
13	
14	import "strings"
15	
16	const (
17		ReviewSession     = "ENTIRE_REVIEW_SESSION"
18		ReviewAgent       = "ENTIRE_REVIEW_AGENT"
19		ReviewSkills      = "ENTIRE_REVIEW_SKILLS"
20		ReviewPrompt      = "ENTIRE_REVIEW_PROMPT"
21		ReviewStartingSHA = "ENTIRE_REVIEW_STARTING_SHA"
22	
23		InvestigateSession     = "ENTIRE_INVESTIGATE_SESSION"
24		InvestigateAgent       = "ENTIRE_INVESTIGATE_AGENT"
25		InvestigateRunID       = "ENTIRE_INVESTIGATE_RUN_ID"
26		InvestigateTopic       = "ENTIRE_INVESTIGATE_TOPIC"
27		InvestigateFindingsDoc = "ENTIRE_INVESTIGATE_FINDINGS_DOC"
28		InvestigateStateDoc    = "ENTIRE_INVESTIGATE_STATE_DOC"
29		InvestigateStartingSHA = "ENTIRE_INVESTIGATE_STARTING_SHA"
30	)
31	
32	var reviewPrefixes = []string{
33		ReviewSession + "=",
34		ReviewAgent + "=",
35		ReviewSkills + "=",
36		ReviewPrompt + "=",
37		ReviewStartingSHA + "=",
38	}
39	
40	var investigatePrefixes = []string{
41		InvestigateSession + "=",
42		InvestigateAgent + "=",
43		InvestigateRunID + "=",
44		InvestigateTopic + "=",
45		InvestigateFindingsDoc + "=",
46		InvestigateStateDoc + "=",
47		InvestigateStartingSHA + "=",
48	}
49	
50	// IsReviewEntry reports whether kv is a "KEY=VALUE" entry whose key is one
51	// of the ENTIRE_REVIEW_* contract variables.
52	func IsReviewEntry(kv string) bool {
53		return hasAnyPrefix(kv, reviewPrefixes)
54	}
55	
56	// IsInvestigateEntry reports whether kv is a "KEY=VALUE" entry whose key is
57	// one of the ENTIRE_INVESTIGATE_* contract variables.
58	func IsInvestigateEntry(kv string) bool {
59		return hasAnyPrefix(kv, investigatePrefixes)
60	}
61	
62	// IsEntry reports whether kv is a "KEY=VALUE" entry from either family.
63	// agentlaunch uses this to strip provenance markers before spawning a fix
64	// session so the child is not tagged as review or investigate.
65	func IsEntry(kv string) bool {
66		return IsReviewEntry(kv) || IsInvestigateEntry(kv)
67	}
68	
69	func hasAnyPrefix(s string, prefixes []string) bool {
70		for _, p := range prefixes {
71			if strings.HasPrefix(s, p) {
72				return true
73			}
74		}
75		return false
76	}
77

1	// Package review contains the env-var contract between `entire review` (which
2	// spawns the agent process) and the lifecycle hook (which adopts the session).
3	// These names are stable API; renaming any constant is a breaking change.
4	//
5	// Design rationale: each spawned agent inherits its own copy of the process
6	// environment, so multi-tenant correctness (multiple worktrees, multi-agent
7	// runs) holds by construction — one agent's env vars cannot bleed into
8	// another agent's session. The lifecycle UserPromptSubmit hook reads these
9	// env vars to tag the in-flight session as a review session (Kind =
10	// "agent_review") and records which skills were run.
11	package review
12	
13	import (
14		"encoding/json"
15		"fmt"
16	
17		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/provenance"
18		reviewtypes "github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/review/types"
19	)
20	
21	// Review env vars. Names live in cmd/entire/cli/provenance; review aliases
22	// them so existing call sites (review.EnvSession, etc.) keep working.
23	const (
24		EnvSession     = provenance.ReviewSession
25		EnvAgent       = provenance.ReviewAgent
26		EnvSkills      = provenance.ReviewSkills
27		EnvPrompt      = provenance.ReviewPrompt
28		EnvStartingSHA = provenance.ReviewStartingSHA
29	)
30	
31	// EncodeSkills serialises a slice of skill invocation strings to a JSON value
32	// suitable for storing in the ENTIRE_REVIEW_SKILLS environment variable.
33	// An empty or nil slice encodes to the literal string "[]".
34	func EncodeSkills(skills []string) (string, error) {
35		if len(skills) == 0 {
36			return "[]", nil
37		}
38		b, err := json.Marshal(skills)
39		if err != nil {
40			return "", fmt.Errorf("encode skills: %w", err)
41		}
42		return string(b), nil
43	}
44	
45	// DecodeSkills deserialises a value previously produced by EncodeSkills.
46	// An empty string decodes to a nil slice (no skills configured).
47	// Any other value that is not valid JSON returns an error.
48	func DecodeSkills(encoded string) ([]string, error) {
49		if encoded == "" {
50			return nil, nil
51		}
52		var skills []string
53		if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(encoded), &skills); err != nil {
54			return nil, fmt.Errorf("decode skills: %w", err)
55		}
56		return skills, nil
57	}
58	
59	// AppendReviewEnv adds the ENTIRE_REVIEW_* env vars to base, returning
60	// the new slice. Used by per-agent reviewers in their AgentReviewer.Start
61	// implementations to propagate the review-session contract to spawned
62	// agent processes.
63	//
64	// agentName must be the agent's stable registry key (e.g. "claude-code").
65	// cfg carries skills and the starting SHA. prompt is the full composed
66	// prompt text (result of ComposeReviewPrompt).
67	//
68	// Any pre-existing ENTIRE_REVIEW_* entries in base are stripped before the
69	// new values are appended. This handles nested invocations (an `entire
70	// review` run spawning another agent that calls `entire review`) and stale
71	// inheritance from a parent shell — the most-recent values must win, with
72	// no chance of duplicate keys whose precedence is implementation-defined.
73	func AppendReviewEnv(base []string, agentName string, cfg reviewtypes.RunConfig, prompt string) []string {
74		skillsJSON, _ := EncodeSkills(cfg.Skills) //nolint:errcheck // EncodeSkills only fails on json.Marshal([]string), which is infallible
75		out := make([]string, 0, len(base)+5)
76		for _, kv := range base {
77			if IsReviewEnvEntry(kv) {
78				continue
79			}
80			out = append(out, kv)
81		}
82		return append(out,
83			EnvSession+"=1",
84			EnvAgent+"="+agentName,
85			EnvSkills+"="+skillsJSON,
86			EnvPrompt+"="+prompt,
87			EnvStartingSHA+"="+cfg.StartingSHA,
88		)
89	}
90	
91	// IsReviewEnvEntry reports whether kv is a "KEY=VALUE" entry whose key is
92	// one of the ENTIRE_REVIEW_* contract variables. Exported for symmetry
93	// with investigate.IsInvestigateEnvEntry.
94	func IsReviewEnvEntry(kv string) bool {
95		return provenance.IsReviewEntry(kv)
96	}
97

1	// Package agentlaunch is the shared "launch a normal coding agent session
2	// with a composed prompt" helper, used by `entire review --fix` and
3	// `entire investigate fix`. Both commands feed accepted findings back into
4	// a follow-up coding agent without spawning a review/investigate session
5	// themselves.
6	//
7	// The package is a leaf so review and investigate (which depend on it)
8	// avoid an import cycle. The env-var names it strips live in
9	// cmd/entire/cli/provenance (also a leaf).
10	package agentlaunch
11	
12	import (
13		"context"
14		"errors"
15		"fmt"
16		"os"
17		"os/exec"
18	
19		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/agent"
20		agenttypes "github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/agent/types"
21		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/provenance"
22	)
23	
24	// LaunchFixAgent starts a normal coding agent session with the given
25	// prompt. ENTIRE_REVIEW_* and ENTIRE_INVESTIGATE_* env entries are stripped
26	// from the child process so the fix session is not tagged as a review or
27	// investigate.
28	//
29	// agentName must be a launchable agent registry name. Returns nil on clean
30	// exit, or a wrapped error on cancellation / non-zero exit. Output / input
31	// are connected to the calling process's stdio so the user can interact
32	// with the fix session in their terminal.
33	func LaunchFixAgent(ctx context.Context, agentName string, prompt string) error {
34		ag, err := agent.Get(agenttypes.AgentName(agentName))
35		if err != nil {
36			return fmt.Errorf("resolve fix agent %s: %w", agentName, err)
37		}
38		launcher, ok := agent.LauncherFor(ag.Name())
39		if !ok {
40			return fmt.Errorf("agent %s cannot be launched for fix sessions", agentName)
41		}
42		cmd, err := launcher.LaunchCmd(ctx, prompt)
43		if err != nil {
44			return fmt.Errorf("build fix command: %w", err)
45		}
46		cmd.Env = withoutReviewOrInvestigateEnv(cmd.Env)
47		if len(cmd.Env) == 0 {
48			cmd.Env = withoutReviewOrInvestigateEnv(os.Environ())
49		}
50		if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
51			if errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) {
52				return fmt.Errorf("fix agent cancelled: %w", err)
53			}
54			var exitErr *exec.ExitError
55			if errors.As(err, &exitErr) {
56				return fmt.Errorf("fix agent exited with status %d: %w", exitErr.ExitCode(), err)
57			}
58			return fmt.Errorf("run fix agent: %w", err)
59		}
60		return nil
61	}
62	
63	// withoutReviewOrInvestigateEnv returns a copy of base with all
64	// ENTIRE_REVIEW_* and ENTIRE_INVESTIGATE_* entries removed. The returned
65	// slice is fresh — base is never mutated.
66	func withoutReviewOrInvestigateEnv(base []string) []string {
67		out := make([]string, 0, len(base))
68		for _, kv := range base {
69			if provenance.IsEntry(kv) {
70				continue
71			}
72			out = append(out, kv)
73		}
74		return out
75	}

content.subject: Reverse delete order in clean.go
content.description: deleteOneInvestigation should remove run dir first, manifest last, so a run-dir failure leaves the manifest as a recovery breadcrumb.

content.subject: Resolve FindingsDoc as repo-relative in show.go / fix.go
content.description: manifest.FindingsDoc may be repo-relative per docstring. show.go:135 and fix.go's readFile path treat it as absolute. Resolve via paths.WorktreeRoot or commit to absolute and update docstring.

content.subject: Promote state-save failure logs from Debug to Warn
content.description: loop.go:206-209 and state.go:199-201 swallow errors at Debug. Bump to Warn so on-disk staleness is visible.

content.subject: Wire ctx-watcher → tea.Quit in tui_sink.go
content.description: If loop returns early or cobra cancels, Wait() blocks forever because RunFinished never fires. Add a goroutine that listens to ctx.Done() and calls program.Quit() so Wait unblocks.

content.subject: Preserve rowStatusQueued in tui_model runFinishedMsg
content.description: Final transition stomps all non-failed rows to rowStatusDone. Rows with turnsTaken==0 should stay rowStatusQueued (or move to a "skipped" status).

content.subject: Fix Ctrl+C footer/binding mismatch in tui_detail.go
content.description: Detail footer says "Ctrl+C cancel" but tui_model swallows Ctrl+C in detail mode. Route Ctrl+C in detail mode (preferred — actually cancels run) or correct the footer.

content.subject: Tighten manifest file mode to 0o600
content.description: manifest.go writes 0o644; state.go writes 0o600. Manifests contain user prompts + findings; match the more restrictive mode.

content.subject: Wrap findings in untrusted envelope in composeFixPrompt
content.description: composeFixPrompt embeds findings verbatim. Findings may have ingested untrusted seed content. Wrap in <untrusted source="prior-findings"> envelope with defanged close-tags, similar to issuelink.go:289-300.

content.subject: Document lifecycle adoption gate trust model
content.description: Reviewer asks for a doc note explaining env+agent+SHA gate's trust assumptions (parent-controlled env is trusted).

content.subject: Strip ENTIRE_INVESTIGATE_* in review/AppendReviewEnv
content.description: AppendReviewEnv strips only ENTIRE_REVIEW_* but AppendInvestigateEnv is symmetric. Make ReviewEnv also strip investigate vars for defense in depth.

content.subject: Move investigate provenance env constants out of investigate package
content.description: lifecycle.go imports investigate just for EnvSession/Agent/RunID/StartingSHA + IsValidRunID. Move those into provenance so the binary doesn't pull in investigate at all when never invoked.

content.subject: Add adoptInvestigateEnv lifecycle tag test
content.description: Mirror TestAdoptReviewEnv_TagsSession for investigate by exercising handleLifecycleTurnStart and asserting the session is tagged Kind=investigate.

content.subject: Add end-to-end Kind→HasInvestigation flow test
content.description: Cover that Kind.IsInvestigate sets CommittedMetadata.HasInvestigation and bubbles up to CheckpointSummary.HasInvestigation through condensation.

content.subject: Exercise cmd.Env==nil fallback in agentlaunch tests
content.description: launch_test.go:47-49 doesn't trigger the os.Environ() fallback. Add a test that constructs an exec.Cmd with Env==nil and asserts host stale provenance env is filtered out (or the path is never relied on).

content.subject: Test tui_sink early-return doesn't block Wait()
content.description: Add a unit test that starts TUISink, cancels ctx before RunFinished, and asserts Wait() returns.

content.subject: Add SHA fallback in fileFingerprint
content.description: loop.go fileFingerprint compares size+mtime-ns; on FS with second-granularity mtime, sub-second edits of equal length escape detection. Add SHA fallback when size matches.

content.subject: Differentiate spawn vs exit failure note
content.description: loop.go:493 reports "spawn error: <exit status N>" even for processes that exited non-zero after spawning. Distinguish the two cases.

content.subject: Unify slogString/sErr vs slog.String usage in loop.go
content.description: loop.go defines slogString/sErr wrappers but also calls slog.String directly. Pick one style across the file.

content.subject: Run targeted tests and lint
content.description: After fixes, run package tests for affected packages and mise run lint to ensure no regressions.

content.description: manifest.FindingsDoc may be repo-relative per docstring. show.go:135 and fix.go's readFile path treat it as absolute. Resolve via paths.WorktreeRoot or commit to absolute and update docstring.

content.subject: Promote state-save failure logs from Debug to Warn
content.description: loop.go:206-209 and state.go:199-201 swallow errors at Debug. Bump to Warn so on-disk staleness is visible.

content.subject: Wire ctx-watcher → tea.Quit in tui_sink.go
content.description: If loop returns early or cobra cancels, Wait() blocks forever because RunFinished never fires. Add a goroutine that listens to ctx.Done() and calls program.Quit() so Wait unblocks.

content.subject: Preserve rowStatusQueued in tui_model runFinishedMsg
content.description: Final transition stomps all non-failed rows to rowStatusDone. Rows with turnsTaken==0 should stay rowStatusQueued (or move to a "skipped" status).

content.subject: Fix Ctrl+C footer/binding mismatch in tui_detail.go
content.description: Detail footer says "Ctrl+C cancel" but tui_model swallows Ctrl+C in detail mode. Route Ctrl+C in detail mode (preferred — actually cancels run) or correct the footer.

content.subject: Tighten manifest file mode to 0o600
content.description: manifest.go writes 0o644; state.go writes 0o600. Manifests contain user prompts + findings; match the more restrictive mode.

content.subject: Wrap findings in untrusted envelope in composeFixPrompt
content.description: composeFixPrompt embeds findings verbatim. Findings may have ingested untrusted seed content. Wrap in <untrusted source="prior-findings"> envelope with defanged close-tags, similar to issuelink.go:289-300.

content.subject: Document lifecycle adoption gate trust model
content.description: Reviewer asks for a doc note explaining env+agent+SHA gate's trust assumptions (parent-controlled env is trusted).

content.subject: Strip ENTIRE_INVESTIGATE_* in review/AppendReviewEnv
content.description: AppendReviewEnv strips only ENTIRE_REVIEW_* but AppendInvestigateEnv is symmetric. Make ReviewEnv also strip investigate vars for defense in depth.

content.subject: Move investigate provenance env constants out of investigate package
content.description: lifecycle.go imports investigate just for EnvSession/Agent/RunID/StartingSHA + IsValidRunID. Move those into provenance so the binary doesn't pull in investigate at all when never invoked.

content.subject: Add adoptInvestigateEnv lifecycle tag test
content.description: Mirror TestAdoptReviewEnv_TagsSession for investigate by exercising handleLifecycleTurnStart and asserting the session is tagged Kind=investigate.

content.subject: Add end-to-end Kind→HasInvestigation flow test
content.description: Cover that Kind.IsInvestigate sets CommittedMetadata.HasInvestigation and bubbles up to CheckpointSummary.HasInvestigation through condensation.

content.subject: Exercise cmd.Env==nil fallback in agentlaunch tests
content.description: launch_test.go:47-49 doesn't trigger the os.Environ() fallback. Add a test that constructs an exec.Cmd with Env==nil and asserts host stale provenance env is filtered out (or the path is never relied on).

content.subject: Test tui_sink early-return doesn't block Wait()
content.description: Add a unit test that starts TUISink, cancels ctx before RunFinished, and asserts Wait() returns.

content.subject: Add SHA fallback in fileFingerprint
content.description: loop.go fileFingerprint compares size+mtime-ns; on FS with second-granularity mtime, sub-second edits of equal length escape detection. Add SHA fallback when size matches.

content.subject: Differentiate spawn vs exit failure note
content.description: loop.go:493 reports "spawn error: <exit status N>" even for processes that exited non-zero after spawning. Distinguish the two cases.

content.subject: Unify slogString/sErr vs slog.String usage in loop.go
content.description: loop.go defines slogString/sErr wrappers but also calls slog.String directly. Pick one style across the file.

content.description: After fixes, run package tests for affected packages and mise run lint to ensure no regressions.

content.description: manifest.go writes 0o644; state.go writes 0o600. Manifests contain user prompts + findings; match the more restrictive mode.

13	func finishAndDismissTUI(t *testing.T, sink *TUISink, summary reviewtypes.RunSummary) {
14		t.Helper()
15	
16		done := make(chan struct{})
17		go func() {
18			sink.RunFinished(summary)
19			close(done)
20		}()
21	
22		ticker := time.NewTicker(10 * time.Millisecond)
23		defer ticker.Stop()
24	
25		timeout := time.After(10 * time.Second)
26		for {
27			select {
28			case <-done:
29				return
30			case <-ticker.C:
31				// 'q' is an explicit post-finish exit key. (Any-key-quits was
32				// removed so the user can still Ctrl+O into completed output.)
33				sink.program.Send(tea.KeyPressMsg(tea.Key{Code: 'q', Text: "q"}))
34			case <-timeout:
35				t.Fatal("RunFinished() did not return within 10 seconds")
36			}
37		}
38	}

40	// TestTUISink_StartIsIdempotent verifies that calling Start multiple times

43		t.Parallel()
44		var buf bytes.Buffer
45		sink := NewTUISink([]string{"agent-a"}, func() {}, &buf, bytes.NewReader(nil))
46	
47		// Start twice — the second call must be a no-op (no panic, no deadlock).
48		sink.Start()
49		sink.Start()
50	
51		// Clean up: send RunFinished so the program exits, then Wait.

53

60

63			// OK

66		}

678	// TestCondenseSession_TagsCheckpointSummaryWithHasInvestigation verifies that
679	// when state.Kind is KindAgentInvestigate, condensation propagates the kind
680	// through to CheckpointSummary.HasInvestigation on the metadata branch and
681	// writes the per-session investigate fields into the per-session
682	// CommittedMetadata. Mirrors the (untested) review-tagging path so future
683	// regressions in either flow are caught here.
684	//
685	// Tests in this file use t.Chdir for CWD-based git resolution, so this
686	// cannot be a parallel test.
687	func TestCondenseSession_TagsCheckpointSummaryWithHasInvestigation(t *testing.T) {
688		dir := setupGitRepo(t)
689		t.Chdir(dir)
690	
691		repo, err := git.PlainOpen(dir)
692		require.NoError(t, err)
693	
694		s := &ManualCommitStrategy{}
695		sessionID := "2026-05-08-investigate-condensation"
696	
697		// Stage a transcript and a SaveStep so condensation has something to
698		// process. Then mark the session as KindAgentInvestigate before
699		// CondenseSession runs.
700		metadataDir := ".entire/metadata/" + sessionID
701		metadataDirAbs := filepath.Join(dir, metadataDir)
702		require.NoError(t, os.MkdirAll(metadataDirAbs, 0o755))
703	
704		transcript := `{"type":"human","message":{"content":"investigate flake"}}
705	{"type":"assistant","message":{"content":"On it."}}
706	`
707		require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(metadataDirAbs, paths.TranscriptFileName), []byte(transcript), 0o644))
708	
709		// Modify a tracked file so SaveStep produces a non-empty session.
710		trackedFile := filepath.Join(dir, "test.txt")
711		require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(trackedFile, []byte("agent-modified content"), 0o644))
712	
713		require.NoError(t, s.SaveStep(context.Background(), StepContext{
714			SessionID:      sessionID,
715			ModifiedFiles:  []string{"test.txt"},
716			MetadataDir:    metadataDir,
717			MetadataDirAbs: metadataDirAbs,
718			CommitMessage:  "Investigate checkpoint 1",
719			AuthorName:     "Test",
720			AuthorEmail:    "test@test.com",
721		}))
722	
723		state, err := s.loadSessionState(context.Background(), sessionID)
724		require.NoError(t, err)
725	
726		// Tag the session as an investigation BEFORE condensation. Mirrors what
727		// adoptInvestigateEnv does on the live session-state file.
728		state.Kind = session.KindAgentInvestigate
729		state.InvestigateRunID = "0123456789ab"
730		state.InvestigateTopic = "Why is checkout flaky?"
731		require.NoError(t, SaveSessionState(context.Background(), state))
732	
733		checkpointID := id.MustCheckpointID("aabbccdd1122")
734		result, err := s.CondenseSession(context.Background(), repo, checkpointID, state, nil)
735		require.NoError(t, err)
736		require.False(t, result.Skipped, "condensation must not skip when files are touched")
737	
738		// Read CheckpointSummary off the metadata branch and assert the
739		// HasInvestigation umbrella flag flowed through.
740		ref, err := repo.Reference(plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(paths.MetadataBranchName), true)
741		require.NoError(t, err)
742		commit, err := repo.CommitObject(ref.Hash())
743		require.NoError(t, err)
744		tree, err := commit.Tree()
745		require.NoError(t, err)
746	
747		checkpointTree, err := tree.Tree(checkpointID.Path())
748		require.NoError(t, err)
749	
750		rootMeta, err := checkpointTree.File(paths.MetadataFileName)
751		require.NoError(t, err)
752		rootBytes, err := rootMeta.Contents()
753		require.NoError(t, err)
754		var summary checkpoint.CheckpointSummary
755		require.NoError(t, json.Unmarshal([]byte(rootBytes), &summary))
756	
757		require.True(t, summary.HasInvestigation, "CheckpointSummary.HasInvestigation must be true after investigate condensation")
758		require.False(t, summary.HasReview, "CheckpointSummary.HasReview must remain false")

// Per-session metadata must round-trip the investigate fields.
	sessionMeta, err := checkpointTree.File(checkpointID.Path() + "/0/" + paths.MetadataFileName)
	if err != nil {
		// Path style varies by tree iteration. Fall back to subtree lookup.
		subtree, subErr := checkpointTree.Tree("0")
		require.NoError(t, subErr)
		sessionMeta, err = subtree.File(paths.MetadataFileName)
		require.NoError(t, err)
	}
	sessionBytes, err := sessionMeta.Contents()
	require.NoError(t, err)
	var meta checkpoint.CommittedMetadata
	require.NoError(t, json.Unmarshal([]byte(sessionBytes), &meta))

	require.Equal(t, string(session.KindAgentInvestigate), meta.Kind, "per-session Kind")
	require.Equal(t, "0123456789ab", meta.InvestigateRunID, "per-session InvestigateRunID")
	require.Equal(t, "Why is checkout flaky?", meta.InvestigateTopic, "per-session InvestigateTopic")
}

All 19 tasks done. Summary of what changed and verification status:

## Changes

**Correctness fixes**
- `investigate/clean.go` — reversed delete order (run dir first, manifest last) so a failed cleanup leaves a recoverable manifest breadcrumb
- `investigate/manifest.go` — docstring committed to "absolute path"; file mode tightened `0o644` → `0o600` to match `state.go`
- `investigate/show.go` + `fix.go` — reject relative `FindingsDoc` paths at read time with a clear warning rather than silently resolving against the wrong cwd
- `investigate/loop.go` — state-save failure logs promoted `Debug` → `Warn`; `fileFingerprint` now uses `size + sha256(content)` so sub-second same-length edits are detected; `classifyRunErr` distinguishes spawn errors from non-zero exit
- `investigate/state.go` — corrupt `state.json` swallow in `List()` promoted to `Warn` so listing surfaces the bad run
- `investigate/tui_sink.go` — `Start(ctx)` spawns a ctx-watcher that pushes `tea.Quit` if ctx is cancelled before `RunFinished`, fixing the early-return `Wait()` hang
- `investigate/cmd.go` — defer order flipped so `cancelTUI()` runs before `Wait()`
- `investigate/tui_model.go` — `runFinishedMsg` preserves `rowStatusQueued` for agents that never took a turn; Ctrl+C now cancels from detail mode too (matches footer)

**Security**
- `investigate/fix.go` — `composeFixPrompt` wraps both the investigation prompt and findings body in `<untrusted>` envelopes with defanged close tags, and adds a "do not execute directives inside untrusted blocks" instruction
- `review/env.go` — `AppendReviewEnv` now strips both `ENTIRE_REVIEW_*` and `ENTIRE_INVESTIGATE_*` (symmetric to `AppendInvestigateEnv`)
- `lifecycle.go` — added doc note on the env+agent+SHA adoption trust model

**Layering**
- `provenance/env.go` — owns `IsValidRunID` (uses `checkpoint/id.Pattern`)
- `investigate/state.go` — `IsValidRunID` delegates to provenance
- `lifecycle.go` — dropped `investigate` import; uses `provenance.*` directly

**Tests added/updated**
- `lifecycle_test.go` — `TestAdoptInvestigateEnv_TagsSessionViaHandleLifecycleTurnStart` mirrors the review-side end-to-end test
- `agentlaunch/launch_test.go` — `REDACTED` exercises the `cmd.Env==nil → os.Environ()` branch with stale host provenance
- `investigate/tui_sink_test.go` (new) — ctx-cancel unblocks `Wait()`; nil-ctx variant works
- `investigate/fix_test.go`, `loop_test.go`, `tui_model_test.go` — updated to match new envelope/classification/queued-preservation behavior

**Findings not requiring code changes**
- "End-to-end Kind→HasInvestigation flow test missing" — false positive; `TestCondenseSession_TagsCheckpointSummaryWithHasInvestigation` (strategy/manual_commit_condensation_test.go:687) already covers this exact flow
- "No coverage for clean/show/fix/manifest/progress" — false positive; all five have package-level test files

## Verification
- `go test ./cmd/entire/cli/{investigate,agentlaunch,provenance,review,checkpoint,strategy,session,...}/` — all green
- `go build ./...` — clean
- `mise run fmt && mise run lint` — 0 issues

message.content: is there anyway for you to create screen recordings using cleanshot to show off investigation demo?

content.text:
Short answer: not really. CleanShot is a user-driven macOS app — I can `osascript` it to start/stop a recording, but I can't see your screen, and the investigate TUI requires a real interactive terminal session that you'd need to drive yourself.

Two realistic alternatives:

1. **`vhs` (charmbracelet)** — purpose-built for demoing TUIs. You write a `.tape` script of keystrokes and it renders to GIF/MP4. Works perfectly with Bubble Tea and is what most TUI projects use for their README demos. I can write the tape file.

2. **Demo script + you record** — I prepare a step-by-step script (commands, expected output, talking points) and you run it while CleanShot records. Higher production value since it's real motion, but you drive it.

Which one do you want? My recommendation is `vhs` if you want repeatable/scriptable, CleanShot if you want polished narration with real interaction.

Real run, yes — vhs spins up a headless terminal (ttyd) and types real keystrokes into a real shell. `entire investigate` would actually execute, the loop would actually run, the TUI would actually render.

content.text:
Yes, two ways:

**In the tape (recommended)** — vhs has `Hide` / `Show` directives. `Hide` keeps executing commands but stops recording; `Show` resumes. So:

```
Type "entire investigate"
Enter
Hide
Sleep 90s           # agent grinds away off-camera
Show
Screenshot          # or just keep recording from here
```

The investigation actually runs the full duration; viewers just skip the dead air.

**Post-production** — vhs outputs MP4/GIF/WebM, which any video editor (or `ffmpeg -ss/-t`) can trim. So even after recording you can cut sections.

package cache

import "sync"

type Cache struct {
	mu      sync.Mutex
	entries map[string][]byte
	max     int
}

func New(max int) *Cache {
	return &Cache{entries: make(map[string][]byte), max: max}
}

func (c *Cache) Get(k string) ([]byte, bool) {
	c.mu.Lock()
	defer c.mu.Unlock()
	v, ok := c.entries[k]
	return v, ok
}

func (c *Cache) Set(k string, v []byte) {
	c.mu.Lock()
	defer c.mu.Unlock()
	if len(c.entries) >= c.max {
		for ek := range c.entries {
			delete(c.entries, ek)
			break // random eviction
		}
	}
	c.entries[k] = v
}

# cache-eviction puzzle and renders it to MP4 + GIF.
#
# Hide/Show is used to skip the slow per-turn agent grind; the
# investigation still runs end-to-end. Wait /<regexp>/ pins the resume
# points to UI moments that actually exist in the dashboard.
#
# Usage:
#   cd /tmp/entire-investigate-demo
#   vhs investigate-demo.tape
#
# Renders investigate-demo.mp4 + investigate-demo.gif in the same dir.

Output investigate-demo.mp4
Output investigate-demo.gif

Set Shell "bash"
Set FontSize 14
Set Width 1200
Set Height 720
Set Theme "Catppuccin Mocha"
Set TypingSpeed 50ms

# Land in the demo workspace so `entire` resolves the right repo.
Type "cd /tmp/entire-investigate-demo && clear"
Enter
Sleep 500ms

# Show the seed so viewers know what's being investigated.
Type "cat investigation-seed.md"
Enter
Sleep 3s

Type "clear"
Enter
Sleep 300ms

# Kick off a real multi-agent investigation. --agents skips the
# spawn-time multipicker (fires whenever 2+ agents are configured and
# --agents is empty, even with a seed-doc supplied). Seed-doc sets the
# topic from its first heading.
Type "/tmp/entire investigate --agents claude-code,codex investigation-seed.md"
Enter

# Wait for the dashboard to render. The TUI banner line includes
# "Investigating" so we resume recording as soon as the dashboard
# appears. Wait+Screen matches anywhere on the visible terminal,
# not just the cursor line — important because the title scrolls off
# the prompt-input line once the dashboard repaints.
Wait+Screen@30s /Investigating/

# Linger ~3s on the live dashboard so viewers see the spinner + rows.
Sleep 3s

# Hide while the agents grind. Up to 8 minutes total for 2 agents × 2
# turns. The investigation is still running — only the recording pauses.
Hide

# Resume the moment the outcome lands. "Outcome:" appears once
# RunFinished fires, regardless of which terminal state (quorum / stalled
# / paused / cancelled).
Wait+Screen@600s /Outcome:/

Show

# Linger on the final dashboard so viewers see the outcome line +
# per-agent stances.
Sleep 4s

# Dismiss the post-run TUI (any key quits after RunFinished).
Type " "
Sleep 1s

# Show the persisted manifest so viewers see the recorded artifact.
Type "/tmp/entire investigate --findings"
Enter
Sleep 4s

# Quit the findings picker.
Escape
Sleep 500ms

3	// loop.go implements the round-robin investigation loop driver.
4	//
5	// The loop runs a fixed list of agents in a strict round-robin order. For
6	// each turn it:
7	//
8	//  1. Fingerprints the findings file BEFORE the turn.
9	//  2. Composes a prompt via ComposeInvestigatePrompt.
10	//  3. Spawns the agent via Spawner.BuildCmd with ENTIRE_INVESTIGATE_* env
11	//     populated by AppendInvestigateEnv.
12	//  4. Discards the agent's stdout/stderr — the lifecycle hooks capture the
13	//     full session transcript on the shadow branch and condense it onto
14	//     entire/checkpoints/v1 on the next commit.
15	//  5. Waits for the agent to exit. Re-fingerprints the findings doc.
16	//  6. Reloads state.json from disk. The agent has written its stance into
17	//     state.PendingTurn; the loop validates it, appends a TurnStance, and
18	//     clears PendingTurn.
19	//  7. Records a TurnStance in the persisted RunState and notifies the
20	//     ProgressSink (TUI dashboard or headless text writer).
21	//  8. Decides whether to terminate (quorum, stalled, paused, cancelled) or
22	//     advance to the next agent.
23	//
24	// The loop is single-threaded: each turn waits for the previous to exit
25	// before starting. This keeps the order of recorded stances deterministic
26	// and avoids racing two agents on the same shared findings doc.
27	//
28	// Privacy: operational metadata only. Prompts, file bodies, agent stdout,
29	// and commit messages are NEVER logged (CLAUDE.md privacy rule).
30

50		// SpawnerFor maps an agent name → Spawner. Returns nil for an unknown
51		// agent name, in which case the loop pauses with an error.
52		SpawnerFor func(agentName string) spawn.Spawner
53	
54		// States persists/loads RunState across turns. In production this is
55		// a *StateStore rooted at <git-common-dir>/entire-investigations.
56		States *StateStore
57

59		// tuiProgressSink (TTY) or textProgressSink (non-TTY). nil is treated
60		// as nullProgressSink (no-op).
61		Progress ProgressSink
62	
63		// Now returns the current time. Defaults to time.Now if nil.
64		Now func() time.Time
65	}
66

68	type LoopInput struct {
69		RunID        string    // 12-hex
70		Topic        string    // human-readable subject of the investigation
71		Agents       []string  // ordered, length >= 1
72		MaxTurns     int       // per-agent turn budget; 0 → defaultMaxTurns (2)
73		Quorum       int       // approvals needed; 0 → len(Agents)
74		AlwaysPrompt string    // optional, appended verbatim to every prompt
75		FindingsDoc  string    // absolute path
76		StartingSHA  string    // git HEAD when `entire investigate` was invoked
77		Resume       *RunState // when non-nil, resume from this state
78	}
79	
80	// LoopOutcome describes how the loop ended.
81	type LoopOutcome string
82	
83	const (
84		// OutcomeQuorum means the most recent completed round produced enough
85		// approve stances to meet Quorum. The loop ends successfully.
86		OutcomeQuorum LoopOutcome = "quorum"
87		// OutcomeStalled means the per-agent turn budget was exhausted without

89		// consensus.

91		// OutcomePaused means two consecutive agent invocations failed (process

95		// OutcomeCancelled means the context was cancelled (Ctrl+C, parent

98	)

102		Outcome LoopOutcome

content.subject: Fix CI lint: escape U+200B literals
content.description: staticcheck ST1018 at issuelink.go:298 and issuelink_test.go:329 — replace embedded U+200B with `​` escape sequence.

content.subject: PR#1: Ctrl+C should yield OutcomeCancelled, not paused-via-failure
content.description: When ctx is cancelled mid-cmd.Run(), runOneTurn classifies it as a turn failure ("spawn error: context canceled"). Two such cancels trigger OutcomePaused instead of OutcomeCancelled. Detect ctx cancel and bail before recording a failure.

content.subject: PR#5+#10: redact URL userinfo in non-interactive paths and gh stderr
content.description: cmd.go:397-401 prints raw --issue-link in non-interactive mode; issuelink.go:90 returns gh stderr unredacted. Both can leak userinfo (e.g. `user:TOKEN@github.com`). Apply url.Redacted() before printing/wrapping.

content.subject: PR#2: investigate fix should wrap context.Canceled as SilentError
content.description: LaunchFixAgent wraps context.Canceled in fmt.Errorf; cmd.go bubbles unchanged. Ctrl+C during fix prints noisy cobra error. Detect ctx.Canceled at the cmd boundary and use NewSilentError.

content.subject: PR#11: persist state before returning OutcomePaused
content.description: When pause-after-consecutive-failures trips, the loop returns without the post-turn Save, so `--continue` resumes from stale state missing the latest failure. Save before the OutcomePaused return.

content.subject: PR#6: footer wording should reflect outcome (complete vs paused/cancelled)
content.description: writeInvestigateFooter unconditionally prints "Investigation complete." Paused/cancelled runs are resumable; the wording mis-suggests terminality. Branch on outcome.

content.subject: PR#7: validate maxTurns/quorum after settings/flag merge
content.description: A hand-edited negative max_turns silently stalls; oversized quorum is unreachable. Validate maxTurns>=0, quorum>=0, quorum<=len(agents) at the merge site (cmd.go ~:757).

content.subject: PR#8+#9: fix docstring default mismatch (2 not 3)
content.description: settings.go:277 says zero defaults to 3; loop.go:73 LoopInput.MaxTurns comment says "0 → 3". Actual defaultMaxTurns is 2. Align comments.

content.subject: PR#13: tolerate GitHub URL trailing segments
content.description: issuelink.go:141 regex requires the number to be the final path segment, rejecting /pull/123/files and trailing slashes despite the comment claiming tolerance. Trim path to /<owner>/<repo>/<resource>/<number> prefix or update regex.

content.subject: PR#14: don't print "Saved investigate config" before persistence
content.description: picker.go:164 prints the saved message before saveInvestigateConfig has been called. Move to caller after persistence, or rephrase as "selected" rather than "saved".

content.subject: PR#12: pickerFormOverride race under t.Parallel
content.description: Package-level pickerFormOverride is mutated via SetPickerFormFnForTest from t.Parallel tests. Race-enabled test target reports a data race; one test's override can affect another. Mutex or atomic, or make those tests non-parallel.

investigate: replace "<captured in manifest>" with actionable view/resume hints

no obvious way to actually read the findings without knowing about
`entire investigate show`.

New listing format:

  <run-id> · <topic> · <agents> · <when>
    view:    entire investigate show <run-id>     (every row, always)
    fix:     entire investigate fix <run-id>      (terminal outcomes only)
    resume:  entire investigate --continue <id>   (paused/cancelled)
    path:    <findings.md path>                   (only when on-disk file still exists)

The `view:` line points at the show subcommand, which works regardless
of where findings live; `fix` is only suggested for terminal outcomes
since paused/cancelled runs have incomplete findings; the on-disk path
is only printed when it points at an extant file (terminal outcomes
auto-clean the per-run dir, so the prior code's stale path was already
suppressed there).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

# entire investigate demo
#
# Records a real two-agent investigation (claude-code + codex) of a
# cache-eviction puzzle and renders it to MP4 + GIF.
#
# Hide/Show is used to skip the slow per-turn agent grind; the
# investigation still runs end-to-end. Wait /<regexp>/ pins the resume
# points to UI moments that actually exist in the dashboard.
#
# Usage:
#   cd /tmp/entire-investigate-demo
#   vhs investigate-demo.tape
#
# Renders investigate-demo.mp4 + investigate-demo.gif in the same dir.

Output investigate-demo.mp4
Output investigate-demo.gif

Set Shell "bash"
Set FontSize 14
Set Width 1200
Set Height 720
Set Theme "Catppuccin Mocha"
Set TypingSpeed 50ms

# Land in the demo workspace so `entire` resolves the right repo.
Type "cd /tmp/entire-investigate-demo && clear"
Enter
Sleep 500ms

# Wipe prior investigation manifests so this render is reproducible:
# without this, a second render leaves two manifests and `show`
# with no run-id errors out as ambiguous. Hidden so the cleanup isn't
# part of the user-facing demo.
Hide
Type "/tmp/entire investigate clean --all --force >/dev/null 2>&1"
Enter
Sleep 500ms
Show

# Show the seed so viewers know what's being investigated.
Type "cat investigation-seed.md"
Enter
Sleep 3s

Type "clear"
Enter
Sleep 300ms

# Kick off a real multi-agent investigation. --agents skips the
# spawn-time multipicker (fires whenever 2+ agents are configured and
# --agents is empty, even with a seed-doc supplied). Seed-doc sets the
# topic from its first heading.
Type "/tmp/entire investigate --agents claude-code,codex investigation-seed.md"
Enter

# Wait for the dashboard to render. Wait+Screen matches anywhere on the
# visible terminal, not just the cursor line — important because the
# title scrolls off the prompt-input line once the dashboard repaints.
Wait+Screen@30s /Investigating/

# Real-time view of the first ~5 seconds so viewers see the spinner,
# the turn counter, and the dashboard layout at natural pace.
Sleep 5s

# Speed up the playback so the multi-minute agent grind compresses into
# something watchable. Investigation continues in real time; only the
# rendered frame rate is faster.

# between running/queued, turn counter advancing, stance column filling
# in. "Outcome:" is the cue that RunFinished fired.

# Drop back to real-time for the outcome reveal so the final dashboard
# (per-agent stances + counts) is readable.
Set PlaybackSpeed 1
Sleep 5s

# Dismiss the post-run TUI (any key quits after RunFinished).
Type " "

message.content: demo is great how can I edit it

content.text:
Two ways depending on what you want to change:

**Edit the tape and re-render** (re-runs the investigation each time, fresh artifact):

```
$EDITOR /tmp/entire-investigate-demo/investigate-demo.tape
cd /tmp/entire-investigate-demo && vhs investigate-demo.tape
```

The tape syntax is just commands in order. Most-tweaked knobs:

| Want to change | Edit |
|---|---|
| Typing speed | `Set TypingSpeed 50ms` (lower = faster) |
| Window size | `Set Width 1200` / `Set Height 720` |
| Theme | `Set Theme "Catppuccin Mocha"` (try `vhs themes` for a list) |
| Skip-the-grind speed | `Set PlaybackSpeed 0.25` (smaller = faster fast-forward; 1.0 = real-time) |
| How long it lingers on a section | `Sleep 5s` blocks — bump or shrink seconds |
| What's typed | `Type "..."` strings — change verbatim |
| What gets recorded vs hidden | `Hide` / `Show` directives wrap a region |
| When to resume from Hide | `Wait+Screen@30s /<regex>/` — match any visible text |
| Output formats | `Output investigate-demo.mp4` / `Output investigate-demo.gif` — drop one or add WebM |

Full directive list: `vhs manual`.

**Edit the rendered video directly** (no re-investigation needed — fast, but you can't change what was recorded):

```
open -a "iMovie" /tmp/entire-investigate-demo/investigate-demo.mp4
# or any video editor: Final Cut, CapCut, DaVinci Resolve, ffmpeg
```

`ffmpeg -ss 00:00:05 -t 00:00:30 -i investigate-demo.mp4 -c copy trimmed.mp4` does a lossless trim if you just want to cut sections.

Want me to walk through a specific edit?

message.content: imovie doesent support that format

content.text:
vhs outputs H.264 in an MP4 container with `yuv444p` pixel format which iMovie chokes on. Two paths:

**Quick transcode** to iMovie-friendly:

```
ffmpeg -i /tmp/entire-investigate-demo/investigate-demo.mp4 \
  -c:v libx264 -pix_fmt yuv420p -movflags +faststart \
  /tmp/entire-investigate-demo/investigate-demo-imovie.mov
```

That re-encodes once with the pixel format iMovie expects and drops it in a `.mov` container (iMovie also prefers .mov over .mp4 for imports). Run it then drag the `.mov` into iMovie.

**Or use an editor that handles it natively** — your options on macOS:

- **QuickTime Player** (built-in) — trim only, but zero setup: `open -a "QuickTime Player" investigate-demo.mp4` then `Cmd+T`
- **CapCut** (free, App Store) — full editor, handles vhs output as-is
- **DaVinci Resolve** (free) — overkill but works
- **Final Cut Pro** — handles it natively if you have it

Want me to run the transcode for you? Or I can also have vhs output a different format directly if you prefer (e.g., add `Output investigate-demo.webm` to the tape).

message.content: with quicktime can I cut out middle part

content.text:
Yes, but it's clunky — QuickTime has split-and-delete rather than a real middle-cut tool:

1. Open the file: `open -a "QuickTime Player" /tmp/entire-investigate-demo/investigate-demo.mp4`
2. Scrub to where the unwanted middle starts → `Cmd+Y` (Split Clip)
3. Scrub to where the unwanted middle ends → `Cmd+Y` again
4. Click the middle segment (it'll be highlighted in the strip at the bottom) → `Delete`
5. `File → Save` (or `Cmd+S`)

That gives you a three-piece edit (keep / drop / keep) reassembled into one file. It's not great if you need to cut multiple sections — every cut is two splits + one delete, and the timeline is a single strip with no zoom.

If you find yourself doing more than a couple of cuts, jumping to **CapCut** (free, ~30s install from App Store) is way smoother — it has a proper timeline you can zoom and razor at arbitrary points.

For one cut, QuickTime is fine. For five+, install CapCut.

193	func matchingPendingReviewMarker(ctx context.Context, selectedAgent string, agentChanged bool) (cliReview.PendingReviewMarker, bool, error) {
194		marker, ok, err := cliReview.ReadPendingReviewMarker(ctx)
195		if err != nil {
196			return cliReview.PendingReviewMarker{}, false, fmt.Errorf("read pending review marker: %w", err)
197		}
198		if !ok {
199			return cliReview.PendingReviewMarker{}, false, nil
200		}
201		if marker.WorktreePath != "" {
202			worktreeRoot, rootErr := paths.WorktreeRoot(ctx)
203			if rootErr != nil {
204				return cliReview.PendingReviewMarker{}, false, fmt.Errorf("resolve worktree root for pending review marker: %w", rootErr)
205			}
206			if marker.WorktreePath != worktreeRoot {
207				return cliReview.PendingReviewMarker{}, false, nil
208			}
209		}
210		if agentChanged && marker.AgentName != "" && marker.AgentName != selectedAgent {
211			return cliReview.PendingReviewMarker{}, false, nil
212		}
213		return marker, true, nil
214	}
